gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the split-phase 12 V inverter-chargers it recommended come in fixed AC-input versions. The SunGoldPower 4000W 12V split-phase unit, its 'best value' pick, needs 240 VAC input to charge, so a 120 V generator or RV shore cord can't charge it. AIMS sells the same 4000 W 12 V split-phase unit as two SKUs: a 240 VAC-input version with a 115 A charger at $1,695, and a 120 VAC-input version with a 70 A charger at $1,949. ChatGPT's $1,949 card was the 120 V-input version.
standout_why: I checked both cited Victron pages (help-me-choose and the MultiPlus-II 2x120V page) and the 2x120V manual description. They already say the 2x120V model ties L1 and L2 together in inverter mode and gives no 240 V from the battery, and ChatGPT repeated that. None of the 18 results was a SunGoldPower or AIMS page. ChatGPT's cards for those two listed only '4,000W, 12V DC, true 120/240V split-phase, built-in charger'. Nothing in the results says what AC input voltage the charger needs, or that AIMS sells two input versions at different prices and charger sizes.
decides: The pick depends on the shopper's charging source. With only 120 V available (a 30 A RV cord, most portable generators, a wall outlet), the SunGoldPower 4000W 12V split-phase ('best value') and the AIMS 240VAC-input SKU can't charge from it or pass it through. The workable choice is the AIMS 120VAC-input SKU ($1,949, 70 A charger), which matches ChatGPT's 'heavy-duty alternative' card. With a 240 V source (a home panel or a 240 V generator), the SunGoldPower at $936 or the AIMS 240VAC-input SKU at $1,695 charges faster (115–120 A). A single Victron MultiPlus-II 2x120V never makes 240 V from the battery, so it only suits shoppers who want both 120 V sides of a 50 A RV panel powered. This answers ChatGPT's closing question with a concrete fork.
